findings.finding: All columns from all three file_schemas entries (train.csv 12 cols, test.csv 9 cols, sampleSubmission.csv 2 cols) are present in available_sources. uncovered_columns is empty. casual and registered correctly classified as 'target' sub-targets rather than excluded or direct features. sampleSubmission.csv::count correctly excluded as placeholder zeros with substantive justification. datetime classified as datetime_derived with correct rationale.

datetime is the row_id/join key per spec_parse.json (row_id_column: 'datetime'). Including datetime__ordinal — a monotonically increasing numeric encoding of the full datetime timestamp — is effectively encoding the row position, which can overfit to temporal trends present only in training range (2011-2012) and may not generalize well to test rows (days 20-end, structurally outside train day range within each month). The ordinal also correlates with unobserved secular demand growth, making it a speculative temporal trend feature. It is not flagged experimental, but is higher-risk than the other datetime-derived components.
findings.required_fix: Flag datetime__ordinal as experimental: true so the Step-6A' ablation gate validates its out-of-fold utility before it enters specialist models, OR provide explicit justification for why ordinal generalizes to test days (20+) given train day range is 1-19.

findings.finding: All 8 aggregates are marked fit_on: fold_train_only. Group keys examined for contemporaneous leakage: ['datetime__hour', 'datetime__month', 'datetime__year'] groups across all same-hour+month+year training rows (days 1-19 in fold-train), not isolating individual prediction-period rows. This is a within-period cross-sub-period dataset (not a panel where period is the atomic unit), so grouping by month+year+hour pools training observations from days 1-13 safely — no same-period peek. No FAIL on leakage.

All three within_period_aggregates are flagged experimental: true, ensuring Step-6A' ablation gate validates them. day_filter: 'day <= 13' correctly restricts to early-period rows only, making these safe lag substitutes per the split structure. Rationale is substantive.

Covers direct numeric, categorical encoding (one-hot for season/weather), datetime-derived (comprehensive: year/month/cyclic/quarter/weekofyear/dayofweek/cyclic/is_weekend/hour/cyclic/ordinal), per-fold target aggregates, interactions (7 entries spanning top-influence signal pairs), within-period aggregates as lag substitutes. No text signal exists (text_like_columns empty). No image sidecars. No lag features planned — correctly omitted per influence file (same-month lags unavailable safely). Feature families are comprehensive for this dataset.

The mapping description ('same datetime keys, one-to-one') is correct and consistent with spec_parse, but the literal count means the runtime code must derive this dynamically from the file rather than relying on this plan literal.
